paragraphs.text:
Tyson brushed and stopped to stare;
A tiny tooth was wobbling there.
“My first loose tooth!” he cried with glee.
“A wiggly tooth belongs to me!”

Dad, Alex, said, “Let's see it go—
Just gentle wiggles, nice and slow.”
Theresa smiled, her eyes so bright:
“We'll let it go when time is right.”

“Wiggle, wobble! Won't you fall?”
It would not budge much more at all.
“Let's take a break,” he heard Dad say.
So Tyson dashed outside to play.

The trampoline was round and green,
The bounciest thing he'd ever seen.
Its net zipped shut; Mom watched nearby,
While Tyson bounced beneath the sky.

A little hop! A happy spin!
A breeze tickled his cheek and chin.
He laughed and bounced above the ground;
His tooth slipped out without a sound.

It tumbled past the padded side
And in the grass it went to hide.
No tiny tap. No shout of “Hey!”
He never felt it slip away.

When play was done, he touched his chin.
His tongue explored his toothy grin.
He found a gap! His eyes grew round:
“My tooth is gone—but can't be found!”

They searched the grass; they checked each shoe.
They looked beneath the trampoline, too.
But not a speck of tooth was there.
Tyson sniffled in the evening air.

“No tooth beneath my pillow tonight!
The fairy won't come on her flight!”
Mom hugged him close. Dad held him tight.
“Let's leave a note,” said Mom. “We'll write.”

Dear Tooth Fairy, my tooth came free
While I was bouncing happily.
I didn't notice it fall that day;
It landed somewhere far away.

We searched and searched, but couldn't see
The little tooth that came from me.
Please visit even though it's gone.
Love, Tyson. Then he gave a yawn.

He tucked the note, then climbed in bed.
Mom kissed his cheek; Dad stroked his head.
The moon shone softly, silver-white;
His little room grew still that night.

On whisper-wings, a fairy flew
And read the note that told her true.
“A missing tooth? That's quite all right.
Your note has brought me here tonight.”

She left a dollar, crisp and green,
Beneath his pillow, quite unseen.
At dawn he peeked—then gave a shout:
“She came! She came! It all worked out!”

Theresa laughed; Dad grinned along.
His tooth was lost, but hope stayed strong.
One dollar! One new gap to show!
And one more way for him to grow.

scenes.heading: A note instead of a tooth
A dollar and a brand-new grin
